subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is a pyridine nucleotide consisting of a nicotinamide riboside molecule bound to a phosphate group. It is an intermediate of the NAD+ salvage pathway and, when administered orally or intraperitoneally, is rapidly converted into NAD+ in major metabolic tissues such as the liver and skeletal muscle. In healthy subjects, oral NMN at 250 mg/day for 12 weeks elevated NAD+ levels in whole blood, and a 300 mg dose for 60 days raised serum NAD+/NADH levels by about 38%. In mice, oral NMN was absorbed from the intestine within minutes and produced a consistent increase in hepatic NAD+ at 15 to 30 minutes, showing that NMN acts as a direct biosynthetic precursor that replenishes the cellular NAD+ pool.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is a pyridine nucleoside made of a nicotinamide base attached to a ribose via a beta-N-glycosidic bond, and it functions as a vitamin-like NAD+ precursor known as the third NAD+ vitamin alongside nicotinamide and nicotinic acid. Oral NR robustly elevates NAD+ concentrations, raising blood NAD+ more than twofold (47.75 uM versus 20.90 uM placebo) and boosting NAAD by 4.5-fold and NMN by 1.4-fold without increasing nicotinamide in blood. NR can enter the salvage pathway directly after absorption or be hydrolyzed to nicotinamide by the glycohydrolase CD157 and routed through the Preiss-Handler pathway, and its metabolic effects are largely mediated by replenishing NAD+ to support sirtuin activity.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: CD38
context: CD38 is an ectoenzyme that consumes NAD+ as a substrate and was found to also degrade nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN). Its levels and activity increase with aging, and this age-related upregulation is required for the NAD+ decline and mitochondrial dysfunction seen in old tissues. Because CD38 breaks down NMN, it alters the pharmacokinetics and bioavailability of both NMN and NR precursors. Consequently CD38 regulates the levels of NAD+, NMN, and SIRT1 activity, making it a candidate molecule for controlling neurodegeneration; in mice, CD38 knockdown suppressed axon degeneration, demyelination, and immune cell infiltration after facial nerve axotomy, and NR injection mimicked this protective effect.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: CD73
context: CD73 is an ecto-5'-nucleotidase that sustains NAD+ synthesis by processing extracellular nucleotide precursors. It dephosphorylates nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) into nicotinamide riboside (NR), which can then be taken up by cells, and it also degrades NAD+ into nicotinamide. In cell studies where NAMPT was inhibited, CD73 activity allowed cell viability by maintaining NAD+ synthesis through this extracellular conversion of NMN to NR. This CD73-mediated dephosphorylation is considered a route by which NMN becomes bioavailable for cellular uptake and salvage into NAD+, complementing the direct transporter pathway and highlighting the importance of ecto-enzymes in precursor metabolism.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: CD157
context: CD157, also called bone marrow stromal cell antigen 1 (BST1), is a glycohydrolase that participates in NAD+ precursor metabolism. It hydrolyzes nicotinamide riboside (NR) into nicotinamide (NAM), which is then further metabolized by gut microbiota into nicotinic acid and routed through the Preiss-Handler pathway to NAD+. In addition, CD157 displays base-exchange activity against both NR and niacin riboside (NAR), interconverting amidated and deamidated precursor pathways. This dual activity means CD157 not only diverts NR toward the deamidated route but also links the two branches of NAD+ biosynthesis, providing alternative substrates that maintain intracellular NAD+ levels depending on tissue and dietary context.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: Gut Microbiome
context: The gut microbiome participates in host NAD+ metabolism because intestinal bacteria possess enzymes that convert nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) into nicotinic acid mononucleotide (NAMN) through deamidation, after which NAMN proceeds through the Preiss-Handler pathway toward NAD+ synthesis. Isotope-labeled NMN given orally to rats was partially deamidated by the intestinal microbiota before absorption, and nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide levels rose in the liver, as also seen after NR supplementation. Shats and colleagues reported that NAD+ enhancement by nicotinamide and NR occurred mostly through this microbiota-dependent deamidated pathway, establishing gut bacteria as active metabolic partners that boost mammalian host NAD+ metabolism rather than simple bystanders.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: NAD+ Salvage Pathway
context: The NAD+ salvage pathway is the main recycling system for the oxidized coenzyme, and its principal substrates are the amidated precursors nicotinamide (NAM), nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), and nicotinamide riboside (NR). NR taken up directly from the diet enters cells and is phosphorylated to NMN and adenylated back into NAD+, restoring intracellular levels that fall with aging, overnutrition, and disease. The reduced forms dihydronicotinamide riboside (NRH) and dihydronicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH) have also been shown to promote synthesis. Together with the de novo route from tryptophan and the Preiss-Handler pathway from nicotinic acid, this redundancy lets multiple dietary precursors maintain NAD+ homeostasis across tissues.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: Sirtuins
context: Sirtuins (SIRT1-7) are NAD+-dependent enzymes that use NAD+ as a substrate to catalyze protein deacetylation or mono-ADP-ribosylation, coupling cellular energy status to gene expression and metabolism. The beneficial effects of NMN and NR supplementation are largely attributed to raising NAD+ levels, which enables sirtuin activity and downstream targets such as PGC-1alpha, FOXO transcription factors, and mitochondrial genes. SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT3 suppress the activity of NF-kB and the NLRP3 inflammasome through multiple mechanisms, while SIRT6 attenuates NF-kB signaling via H3K9 deacetylation, linking NAD+ precursor intake to anti-inflammatory and longevity-related outcomes in aging, diabetes, and COVID-19 contexts.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: PARP
context: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerases (PARPs) are NAD+-consuming enzymes that transfer ADP-ribose units onto proteins and nucleic acids, playing critical roles in DNA repair and antiviral immunity. During aging, accumulated DNA damage activates PARPs, which depletes NAD+ and reduces SIRT1 activity. In SARS-CoV-2 infection, PARPs inhibit viral transcript translation through ADP-ribosylation, but viral macrodomain proteins hydrolyze these ADPR units, and the compensatory hyperactivation of PARPs consumes NAD+; restoring NAD+ may therefore support the antiviral functions of PARPs. PARPs also consume NAD+ during diabetes-associated DNA repair, contributing to the NAD+/NADH redox imbalance that drives diabetic complications.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: SARM1
context: SARM1 is a NAD+-consuming enzyme, grouped with CD38 and CD157 as an NAD+ glycohydrolase that degrades the coenzyme in signaling and stress pathways. Alongside ADP-ribosyl transferases, poly-ADP polymerases, and sirtuins, SARM1 mediates essential NAD+-dependent processes such as DNA repair, apoptosis, cell survival, lifespan regulation, and metabolic adjustments. Its NAD+ consumption contributes to the constant synthesis-catabolism-recycling cycle that sustains NAD+ levels, and disturbances that shift this balance, such as aging or infection, can reduce NAD+ availability. Dietary precursors like NMN and NR counter this by replenishing the NAD+ pool consumed by these signaling enzymes.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: Aging
context: Aging is associated with a progressive decline in NAD+ levels in various tissues, driven mainly by reduced NAMPT-mediated biosynthesis and by increased activity of the NAD+-consuming ectoenzyme CD38. NAMPT protein and NAD+ levels fall significantly in organs such as white adipose tissue and skeletal muscle of old mice, which impairs the activity of NAD+-dependent enzymes like sirtuins and alters cellular redox balance, leading to functional decline. This age-related NAD+ depletion is a hallmark of physiological decline and is linked to the onset of age-associated diseases including metabolic disorders, neurodegeneration, and ocular conditions, making NAD+ precursors a proposed strategy to mitigate age-associated physiological decline.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: NAMPT
context: NAMPT (nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase) is the rate-limiting enzyme that converts nicotinamide into nicotinamide mononucleotide in the NAD+ salvage pathway. A significant cause of age-associated NAD+ decline is the decrease in NAMPT-mediated biosynthesis: NAMPT protein and NAD+ levels fall in white adipose tissue and skeletal muscle of old mice, reducing the activity of NAD+-dependent enzymes such as sirtuins. Inhibiting NAMPT decreases cell growth and increases susceptibility to oxidative stress, a concept being explored for cancer therapy, whereas NMN and NR bypass NAMPT to reverse the cell death it induces, underscoring NAMPT as the central control point of endogenous NAD+ production.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: DNA Damage
context: During the aging process, DNA damage accumulates in the cell nucleus and activates PARPs, which consume NAD+ as a substrate for poly-ADP-ribosylation during DNA repair. This PARP activation depletes NAD+ levels and consequently reduces SIRT1 activity, contributing to age-related decline. In diabetes, overactivation of PARPs likewise diminishes NAD+ and exacerbates the NAD+/NADH redox imbalance that leads to oxidative stress and diabetic complications. Conversely, NMN treatment in telomere-dysfunction models dampened the DNA damage response and p53 activation, functionally rescuing liver fibrosis and improving mitochondrial biogenesis, showing that NAD+ precursor supplementation can offset the metabolic cost of DNA damage-driven PARP activity.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 is a NAD+-dependent deacetylase that, when activated by rising NAD+ levels, deacetylates and activates the transcriptional coactivator PGC-1alpha. PGC-1alpha in turn co-regulates mitochondrial genes and detoxifying enzymes that eliminate reactive oxygen species, increasing mitochondrial activity and biogenesis and leading to improved metabolism and antioxidant protection. This SIRT1-PGC1alpha axis links NAD+ precursor intake to mitochondrial health, and its targets include the FOXO1 and FOXO3a transcription factors. NR and NMN act through this pathway to improve mitochondrial function, enhance oxidative metabolism and energy expenditure, and protect tissues such as the myocardium against oxidative stress and apoptosis.
source_document: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md

subject: AMPK
context: AMPK is a cellular energy regulator that senses changes in the intracellular AMP/ATP ratio. Under energy limitation, low ATP levels activate AMPK, which switches on catabolic pathways that produce ATP by enhancing oxidative metabolism and mitochondrial biogenesis while switching off ATP-consuming anabolic pathways, thereby altering the NAD+/NADH ratio. By increasing cellular NAD+ levels, AMPK enhances SIRT1 activity, which then deacetylates and modulates energy metabolism-related targets including PGC-1alpha, FOXO1, and FOXO3a. This AMPK-SIRT1-NMNR circuit explains how nutrient and energy status couples to NAD+-dependent regulation, and why NAD+ precursor supplementation can reinforce these energy-sensing pathways.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) promoted telomere lengthening in aged mice, pre-aging mice, and humans. In one study, treating generation-4 mice with NMN in drinking water for 8 weeks lengthened telomeres, dampened the DNA damage response and p53 activation, functionally rescued liver fibrosis, and improved mitochondrial biogenesis and function in a partially SIRT1-dependent manner. The increased NAD+ levels in the liver of NMN-treated mice reversed hyperacetylation of several sirtuin targets, reinforcing sirtuin activity. These effects counteract the telomere shortening and sirtuin repression that accompany DNA damage accumulation, positioning NMN as a nutraceutical candidate to prevent age-related physiological decline.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is an effective intervention against the pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes in both diet-induced and age-induced mouse models. Intraperitoneal administration at 500 mg/kg body weight per day for 11 days substantially ameliorated impaired glucose tolerance and enhanced hepatic insulin sensitivity, with the reversal of gene expression changes related to oxidative stress, inflammatory response, and circadian rhythm partly resulting from SIRT1 activation. NMN also restored glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in aged beta-cell-specific SIRT1-overexpressing (BESTO) mice and aged wild-type mice, and in postmenopausal women with prediabetes, 250 mg/day for 10 weeks increased NAD+ in PBMCs and improved insulin signaling and sensitivity in skeletal muscle.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) improves insulin sensitivity and signaling, particularly in metabolically compromised settings. In postmenopausal women with overweight or obesity and prediabetes, oral NMN at 250 mg/day for 10 weeks increased NAD+ content in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and improved insulin signaling and sensitivity in skeletal muscle. In mouse models, NMN enhanced hepatic insulin sensitivity and ameliorated impaired glucose tolerance, although these benefits were most pronounced in the most metabolically compromised groups. Notably, NMN had no beneficial effect on glucose metabolism in healthy mice on a chow diet and even impaired glucose tolerance in lean-progenitor offspring, suggesting precursors act best when NAD+ levels are depleted.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) restores insulin secretion that is impaired by inflammation and metabolic stress. In islets cultured with the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1beta and TNF-alpha, NMN administration at 100 umol/L restored insulin secretion in a partially SIRT1-dependent manner and corrected inflammation-induced islet dysfunction by reversing changes in genes encoding islet markers essential for glucose sensing and beta-cell differentiation. In mice fed a fructose-rich diet, NMN improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, indicating protection against beta-cell failure through an anti-inflammatory mechanism. This action supports NMN's anti-diabetic effects and its capacity to preserve pancreatic beta-cell function under cytokine-driven stress.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) improves features of Alzheimer's disease by raising NAD+ levels and supporting sirtuin activity. It protects neuronal cells from oxidative stress, prevents beta-amyloid oligomer-induced cognitive impairment and neuronal death, and inhibits JNK activation to reverse Alzheimer's disease pathology in experimental models. NMN is proposed as a nutraceutical to prevent age-related physiological decline and has demonstrated cardio- and vasoprotective actions as well. Alongside nicotinamide riboside, which reduces neuroinflammation, phosphorylated Tau, DNA damage, and hippocampal neuron apoptosis while increasing neurogenesis, NMN represents a dietary NAD+ precursor strategy against neurodegenerative and age-related diseases.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) reduces beta-amyloid levels and protects cognitive function in Alzheimer's disease models. In Tg2576 mice, NR treatment lowered beta-amyloid and increased the chance of recognizing a novel object by 20%, indicating improved recognition memory. NR also significantly reduced neuroinflammation, apoptosis of hippocampal neurons, phosphorylated Tau, and DNA damage, while increasing neurogenesis by almost 20%. These cognitive and synaptic protective effects are attributed to NR's ability to elevate NAD+ and upregulate proliferator-activated receptor-gamma coactivator 1-alpha-regulated beta-secretase 1 degradation and mitochondrial gene expression, linking NAD+ precursor supplementation to preservation of learning, memory, and motor function.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) enhances neurogenesis while reducing neurodegenerative pathology in Alzheimer's disease models. NR treatment increased neurogenesis by almost 20% and simultaneously reduced neuroinflammation, apoptosis of hippocampal neurons, phosphorylated Tau, and DNA damage. These effects protect cognitive function, synaptic plasticity, learning, memory, and motor function in animal models. The mechanisms are attributed to NR raising NAD+ levels, which sustains sirtuin activity and mitochondrial gene expression, and reducing the beta-amyloid burden. This positions NR as a promising NAD+ precursor for counteracting the neuronal loss and cognitive decline associated with aging and Alzheimer's disease.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) reduces neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease models and in alcohol-induced depression models. In AD models, NR significantly reduced neuroinflammation, apoptosis of hippocampal neurons, phosphorylated Tau, and DNA damage while increasing neurogenesis. In mice with alcohol-induced depression, dietary NR for 10 weeks reduced both pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokine levels and inhibited microglial activation, with the protective effect attributed to NR upregulating brain-derived neurotrophic factor by altering gut microbiota composition. These findings connect NR's NAD+-boosting action to suppression of neuroinflammation, microglial reactivity, and preservation of cognitive and emotional function.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) prevents and improves metabolic disorders such as high-fat diet-induced obesity. NR supplementation promoted metabolic flexibility by enhancing energy expenditure, significantly attenuating high-fat diet-induced body weight gain and decreasing fat mass, particularly in the liver where triglyceride levels dropped by 40%. NR also protected against hyperinsulinemia and elevated total and LDL cholesterol caused by a high-fat diet, while having no effect on body weight when given with a normal chow diet. Additionally, NR-conditioned gut microbiota conferred protection against high-fat diet weight gain through fecal transfer, linking the gut microbiome to its anti-obesity effects.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) protects against non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and its metabolic sequelae by increasing NAD+ and stimulating sirtuins. NR supplementation increased hepatic beta-oxidation and mitochondrial content, reversing glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, liver lipid accumulation, and hepatic fibrosis in mouse models. In high-fat diet studies, NR reduced liver fat mass and decreased hepatic triglyceride levels by 40%. These benefits arise from NR elevating NAD+ in liver and muscle, which stimulates SIRT1 and SIRT3 activity to enhance oxidative metabolism and mitochondrial function, counteracting the fatty liver and metabolic inflexibility driven by overnutrition.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) increases energy expenditure and promotes metabolic flexibility. By elevating NAD+ in liver and muscle, NR supplementation stimulated SIRT1 and SIRT3 activity, enhancing mitochondrial function, oxidative metabolism, and endurance performance in mice. NR's enhancement of energy expenditure significantly attenuated high-fat diet-induced body weight gain and decreased fat mass, particularly in the liver. NR also stabilized myocardial NAD+ levels, increasing glycolysis and citrate and acetyl-coenzyme A metabolism, which attenuated the development of heart failure in a dilated cardiomyopathy model. These metabolic effects establish NR as a dietary agent that supports energy homeostasis and protects against overnutrition-driven metabolic disease.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) activates SIRT3 by raising NAD+ levels. A 24-hour administration of NR to peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy subjects replicated the fasting effect of blunting NLRP3 inflammasome activation and enhancing mitochondrial quality control through SIRT3. NR reduced acetylation of SOD2 and isocitrate dehydrogenase 2, increasing mitochondrial SOD2 activity and thereby reducing mitochondrial reactive oxygen species levels. It also decreased secretion of IL-1beta and TNF-alpha in monocytes and macrophages. This SIRT3-dependent mechanism links NR intake to reduced mitochondrial oxidative stress and suppression of the NLRP3 inflammasome, underpinning its anti-inflammatory and metabolic benefits.

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 is the primary mitochondrial NAD+-dependent deacetylase, and among its targets is SOD2 (manganese superoxide dismutase). When NR raises NAD+ and activates SIRT3, the acetylation of SOD2 is reduced, increasing mitochondrial SOD2 activity and thereby lowering mitochondrial reactive oxygen species. SIRT3 also deacetylates isocitrate dehydrogenase 2, enhancing mitochondrial antioxidant capacity and quality control. This SIRT3-SOD2 axis is central to NR's protective effects against oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and it also mediates the benefit of gut-microbiota-derived NMN in acute pancreatitis, where the SIRT3-PRDX5 pathway is engaged.

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3, along with SIRT1 and SIRT2, suppresses the activity of NF-kB and the NLRP3 inflammasome through multiple mechanisms. Because sirtuins are NAD+-dependent, raising NAD+ with precursors such as NR enhances this suppression. In human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, 24-hour NR administration recapitulated the fasting effect of blunting NLRP3 inflammasome activation and enhancing mitochondrial quality control in a SIRT3-dependent manner, reducing secretion of IL-1beta and TNF-alpha. This sirtuin-mediated restraint of the NLRP3 inflammasome helps prevent cytokine storm in severe infections and mitigates the chronic inflammation associated with aging and metabolic disease.

subject: SOD2
context: SOD2 (manganese superoxide dismutase) is the mitochondrial antioxidant enzyme that eliminates superoxide generated during respiration. Its activity is regulated by acetylation, with SIRT3-mediated deacetylation increasing SOD2 activity. When NR raises NAD+ and activates SIRT3, SOD2 acetylation decreases, mitochondrial SOD2 activity rises, and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species levels fall. This reduced mitochondrial ROS burden lessens oxidative damage and supports mitochondrial quality control, contributing to NR's protective effects against oxidative stress, inflammasome activation, and age-related mitochondrial dysfunction in tissues such as the myocardium, skeletal muscle, and neurons.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) decreases secretion of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-1beta in human immune cells. In healthy volunteers, 24-hour NR administration reduced IL-1beta secretion in monocytes by over 50% (from approximately 22,000 to 10,000 pg/mL) and in macrophages by around 20% (from above 300 to less than 250 pg/mL). This effect is mediated by SIRT3-dependent blunting of NLRP3 inflammasome activation and enhanced mitochondrial quality control. By reducing IL-1beta and TNF-alpha production, NR demonstrates systemic anti-inflammatory activity consistent with its NAD+-boosting and sirtuin-activating mechanism.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) reduces circulating and cellular levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokine TNF-alpha. In healthy volunteers, 24-hour NR administration decreased TNF-alpha secretion by over 75% in monocytes (from above 2000 to less than 500 pg/mL) and approximately 45% in macrophages (from around 1800 to 1000 pg/mL). In older men supplementing with 1 g of oral NR per day for 3 weeks, circulating TNF-alpha fell from around 250 to 200 pg/mL along with reductions in IL-2, IL-5, and IL-6. This anti-inflammatory action is mediated through NAD+-dependent sirtuin activation and contributes to NR's cardiovascular, metabolic, and neuroprotective benefits.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) suppresses inflammation and oxidative stress by downregulating cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2). In LPS-activated mouse and human macrophage cell lines (THP-1 and RAW264.7), treatment with 500 uM NMN decreased pro-inflammatory cytokine production and efficiently alleviated LPS-induced inflammation via the COX-2-PGE2 axis. NMN markedly decreased mRNA expression and extracellular secretion of IL-6 and IL-1beta and lowered cellular prostaglandin E2 levels, while proteins related to the inflammatory response such as RELL1, PTGS2, FGA, FGB, and igkv12-44 were reduced. NMN also suppressed prostanoid biosynthesis and NF-kB signaling, demonstrating broad anti-inflammatory activity in innate immune cells.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) suppresses NF-kB signaling as part of its anti-inflammatory mechanism. In LPS-activated macrophages, proteomics analysis identified that NMN downregulated COX-2 expression and suppressed inflammation-related pathways including prostanoid biosynthesis, LPS/IL-1-mediated inhibition of RXR function, and IL-6 and NF-kB signaling. This downregulation of NF-kB and related pathways decreased extracellular secretion of IL-6 and IL-1beta and lowered prostaglandin E2 levels, alleviating LPS-induced inflammation and oxidative stress. These effects complement the sirtuin-mediated suppression of NF-kB, positioning NMN as a dietary agent that restrains the master pro-inflammatory transcription factor.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) exerts cardio- and vasoprotective actions, protecting against heart failure, ischemia, and reperfusion injury. NMN preserves cardiac mitochondrial homeostasis, prevents heart failure in animal models, and attenuates cardiac fibrosis by regulating oxidative stress and Smad3 acetylation. It also restores angiogenic capacity and attenuates oxidative stress in aged cerebromicrovascular endothelial cells, and rescues endothelial dysfunction and neurovascular coupling in aged mice. By inhibiting inflammation and decreasing oxidative stress, NMN prevents arterial and endothelial dysfunction, supporting its proposed use as a nutraceutical against age-related cardiovascular decline.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) preserves cardiac function in heart failure models by stabilizing NAD+ levels. In a mouse model of dilated cardiomyopathy, NR at 450 mg/kg body weight for 45 days stabilized myocardial NAD+ levels, increased glycolysis, and citrate and acetyl-coenzyme A metabolism, attenuating the development of heart failure. NR also elevates myocardium NAD+ content in diabetic mice, promoting mitofusin 2-mediated mitochondrial fusion through the SIRT1-PGC1alpha-PPARalpha pathway, which suppresses oxidative stress and cell apoptosis. These cardiac benefits, combined with its reduction of inflammation and vascular protection, establish NR as a cardioprotective NAD+ precursor.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) promotes mitochondrial fusion, particularly in the diabetic heart. Daily oral gavage of NR at 400 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks alleviated diabetes-induced cardiomyopathy and improved cardiac function in diabetic mice by elevating myocardium NAD+ content and promoting mitofusin 2-mediated mitochondrial fusion. This action occurs via the SIRT1-PGC1alpha-PPARalpha pathway and suppresses oxidative stress and cell apoptosis. By restoring balanced mitochondrial dynamics in a disease state characterized by mitochondrial fragmentation and dysfunction, NR supports cardiomyocyte survival and cardiac bioenergetics.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) derived from the gut microbiota ameliorates acute pancreatitis injury. In acute pancreatitis mouse models, NMN increased NAD+ levels and activated the SIRT3-PRDX5 pathway, mitigating pancreatic mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative damage, and inflammation in a partially SIRT3-dependent manner. Acute pancreatitis is exacerbated by gut microbiota dysbiosis, and normobiotic fecal microbiota transplantation induced higher serum NMN levels, enhancing NAD+ biosynthesis in the pancreas. This makes NMN an important mediator of the protective effects of fecal microbiota transplantation and highlights the role of gut microbiota-produced NAD+ precursors in pathological outcomes of the host.

subject: Gut Microbiome
context: The gut microbiota can produce nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), and this microbe-derived NMN exerts protective effects on host tissues. NMN derived from gut microbiota ameliorated acute pancreatitis by increasing NAD+ levels and activating the SIRT3-PRDX5 pathway in mouse models, and normobiotic fecal microbiota transplantation induced higher NMN levels in serum while enhancing NAD+ biosynthesis in the pancreas. Gut bacteria also produce B vitamins and engage the deamidated NAD+ biosynthesis pathway, and microorganisms in fermented beverages can synthesize NMN and NR. This bidirectional axis positions gut microbes as sources of NAD+ precursors that influence host metabolism and disease outcomes.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) can selectively stimulate the growth of beneficial gut bacteria such as Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus. These genera are associated with improved gut health, including prevention of diarrhea, improved gut barrier function, reduced inflammation, and immune system support. NAD+ precursors modulate gut microbiota by providing an energy source for beneficial bacteria, activating sirtuins, and improving gut barrier function. NMN and NR thereby reverse gut dysbiosis and promote beneficial effects at both intestinal and extraintestinal levels, linking dietary NAD+ precursor intake to a healthier gut microbial community.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) can selectively stimulate the growth of beneficial gut bacteria such as Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus. These bacteria are associated with improved gut health, including prevention of diarrhea, improved gut barrier function, reduced inflammation, and immune support. NR also modulates gut microbiota in ways protective against high-fat diet-induced weight gain: mice fed 60% HFD with 0.4% NR for 168 days had nearly 16% less weight gain and lower fasting blood glucose, and fecal transfer from NR-treated donors reproduced the protective effect with a microbiota enriched in butyrate-producing Firmicutes. NR thus reshapes the microbiome to favor metabolically beneficial bacteria.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Long-term nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation modulates gut microbiota composition in humans, increasing the abundance of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii. In a twin study, NR at 250-1000 mg/day for 5 months raised F. prausnitzii abundance, and association analysis suggested this bacterium contributes to regulation of NAD+, inflammation, amino acid, and lipid metabolism. Faecalibacterium prausnitzii is a butyrate-producing commensal that promotes metabolic health and anti-inflammatory responses, and its decline characterizes dysbiosis in inflammatory bowel disease. NR's ability to enrich this beneficial organism supports its role in improving gut and systemic health through microbiota modulation.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) reverses gut dysbiosis and protects the intestinal tract. In an experimental mouse model of colitis induced by dextran sodium sulfate, NMN given by gavage at 1 mg/g body weight increased microbial abundance and diversity, improved mucus secretion and tight-junction protein expression, and attenuated intestinal mucosal permeability, protecting against inflammatory bowel disease. Long-term NMN treatment modulated gut microbiota diversity and composition, increasing butyric acid-producing bacteria such as Ruminococcaceae UCG-014 and Prevotellaceae NK3B31 as well as Akkermansia muciniphila, while decreasing harmful bacteria like Bilophila and Oscillibacter. NMN thereby restores intestinal homeostasis and barrier integrity through microbiota remodeling.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) improves intestinal barrier function, which is important for preventing translocation of harmful bacteria and toxins from the gut into the bloodstream. In colitis models, NMN increased the expression of tight-junction proteins and improved mucus secretion, attenuating intestinal mucosal permeability. Long-term NMN treatment also increased the number of goblet cells, mucus thickness, and tight junction protein expression, maintaining the integrity of the intestinal epithelium. NMN and NR share this gut-protective property alongside selective stimulation of beneficial bacteria, and NAD+-precursor-activated sirtuins also protect intestinal endothelial cells against oxidative injury, collectively reinforcing the gut barrier.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) protects against alcohol-induced depression-like behaviors in mice by altering gut microbiota composition. Dietary supplementation with NR for 10 weeks at 400 mg/kg daily reduced both pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokine levels, inhibited microglial activation, and provided protection against alcohol-induced depression-like behaviors. The effect was attributed to NR's ability to upregulate brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) through microbiota changes: brain BDNF levels correlated positively with bacteria enriched in the NR group such as Barnesiella, Alloprevotella, Prevotella, Alistipes, and Mucispirillum. Fecal microbiota transplantation from NR-treated donors reproduced the protective features in germ-free recipients, demonstrating a gut-microbiota-gut-brain axis mechanism.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) upregulates brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) by altering gut microbiota composition. In a mouse model of alcohol-induced depression, 10 weeks of NR supplementation reduced pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, inhibited microglial activation, and protected against depression-like behaviors, with the protective effect attributed to NR-driven increases in BDNF. Brain BDNF levels were positively correlated with bacteria abundant in NR-treated mice, such as Barnesiella and Alloprevotella, whereas brain inflammatory cytokines correlated with bacteria enriched in the depression model group. This BDNF upregulation via microbiota remodeling links NR intake to improved emotional behavior and neural plasticity.

subject: Butyrate
context: Butyrate, a short-chain fatty acid produced by gut bacteria such as Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Eubacterium rectale, and Roseburia, reduces adiposity by inhibiting intestinal cholesterol biosynthesis and promoting beneficial metabolic effects including insulin secretion, insulin sensitivity, and energy expenditure. Butyrate can also increase satiety and gut motility by upregulating the expression of peptide YY and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1). In studies where NR supplementation enriched butyrate-producing Firmicutes, these metabolic benefits contributed to protection against high-fat diet-induced weight gain, and fecal transfer reproduced the effect, underscoring butyrate as a key mediator of microbiota-driven metabolic health.

subject: NAD+
context: NAD+ can directly affect the metabolism of intestinal microorganisms. Because NAD+ is an important component in the energy metabolism of all living organisms, mainly as a cofactor for key enzymes involved in cellular ATP production, boosting NAD+ may promote microbial energy production. NAD+ can also indirectly affect gut microbes by regulating the movement of the colon through the key inhibitory neurotransmitter beta-NAD and by affecting the synthesis of host bile acids, which can be antimicrobial when they destroy bacterial cell membranes. These mechanisms complement the ability of NMN and NR to modulate gut microbiota composition, forming a bidirectional NAD+-microbiota axis.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is found in a range of foods including edamame beans, avocado, broccoli, cucumber, cabbage, and tomato, according to the first evidence published by Mills et al. (2016). Among the investigated sources, the highest NMN content was found in edamame at 0.47-1.88 mg/100 g and avocado at 0.36-1.60 mg/100 g, with smaller amounts in seafood and raw meats (0.06-0.42 mg/100 g). Milk also contains NMN, with human milk the richest source at 2.1-9.8 uM. These natural occurrences support the idea that a normal diet can contribute to NAD+ precursor intake, though optimal sources remain to be established.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) was first discovered in milk and, until recently, had only been measured there. Bovine milk contains the highest NR content among milk sources at 0.5-3.6 uM, while human milk is the richest source of nicotinamide mononucleotide at 2.1-9.8 uM. NR and NMN are also determined in different species of milk and beer. The niacin quantified by microbiological assay (AOAC Method 944.13) actually includes NR and NMN, because hot acid or alkaline extraction hydrolyzes these molecules into nicotinic acid, meaning NR and NMN contribute to the measured niacin content of milk and other foods.

subject: Saccharomyces cerevisiae
context: Yeast-mediated production of nicotinamide riboside (NR) and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) was demonstrated in craft beers, with hop indicating a role in enhancing NR levels during fermentation. This finding opens new perspectives for enriched sources of NAD+ precursors through fermented foods and beverages. Additionally, fructophilic lactic acid bacteria have been investigated for biotechnological production of NMN and NR for functional probiotic products and supplements. These microbial routes complement natural dietary sources such as vegetables, meat, milk, and mushrooms, and could enable the development of new functional foods and biotechnological strategies to maintain and enhance the physiological benefits of NAD+ precursors.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: A sub-chronic 90-day toxicity study in rats established that repeated oral administration of synthetic NMN at doses up to 1500 mg/kg/day appears safe and did not promote toxic effects on body weight, food and water consumption, feed conversion efficiency, or biochemical and blood parameters, although higher doses increased kidney, liver, and adrenal gland weights and elevated hepatic enzymes such as alkaline phosphatase, alanine aminotransferase, and aspartate aminotransferase. Based on these findings, the established upper intake level of NMN for a 60 kg individual was set at 900 mg per day. Human studies at 100-500 mg single doses and 250-300 mg/day over weeks to months reported no adverse effects.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is unstable in blood, degrading very rapidly even at -80 degrees Celsius. In the first clinical trial of single oral NMN doses (100-500 mg) in healthy subjects, NMN was not detected in plasma, most likely because sample freezing before extraction caused NMN degradation. This rapid degradation complicates accurate measurement of circulating NMN and may explain why plasma NMN levels are kept low and constant, presumably due to balanced NMN distribution from plasma to tissues. In mice, orally administered NMN was quickly absorbed from the intestine, eliminated from circulation within 15 minutes, and rapidly converted into NAD+ in tissues such as the liver and soleus muscle.

subject: Nicotinamide
context: Although nicotinamide (NAM) effectively increases NAD+ in tissues, it also exerts an inhibitory effect on sirtuins and PARP activity, a property that distinguishes it from the other precursors NMN and NR. At high doses, NAM is methylated by nicotinamide N-methyltransferase to generate N1-methylnicotinamide for elimination in urine, which can lower the cellular methyl pool over time. This depletion could reduce DNA and protein methylation and alter gene expression patterns and protein activity, since DNA methylation in gene promoter regions is typically associated with transcriptional repression. These effects may explain why NR administration raises NAD+ levels more than NAM treatment in some studies.

subject: Nicotinamide
context: Nicotinamide (NAM), the amide form of vitamin B3 and a product released from NAD+-consuming reactions, inhibits PARP activity while being effective at increasing NAD+ levels in tissues. At high doses, NAM is metabolized by nicotinamide N-methyltransferase into N1-methylnicotinamide for urinary elimination, which can progressively lower the cellular methyl pool, potentially reducing DNA and protein methylation and altering gene expression and protein activity. This dual role as both NAD+ precursor and PARP/sirtuin inhibitor distinguishes NAM from NMN and NR, which elevate NAD+ without this inhibitory action, and may explain differences in their metabolic outcomes.

subject: NRH
context: NRH (dihydronicotinamide riboside) is the reduced form of nicotinamide riboside and has recently been shown to promote NAD+ synthesis. Alongside NMNH (dihydronicotinamide mononucleotide), the reduced form of nicotinamide mononucleotide, NRH expands the repertoire of NAD+ precursors beyond the amidated molecules nicotinamide, NMN, and NR. These reduced precursors are additional substrates for the salvage pathway and are considered orally bioavailable NAD+ precursors. Their discovery illustrates the redundancy of NAD+ biosynthetic routes and suggests that multiple dietary and pharmacological compounds can contribute to maintaining intracellular NAD+ levels across tissues.

subject: NMNH
context: NMNH (dihydronicotinamide mononucleotide) is the reduced form of nicotinamide mononucleotide and has been shown to promote NAD+ synthesis. Together with NRH, the reduced form of nicotinamide riboside, NMNH adds to the set of NAD+ precursors available for cellular salvage and NAD+ replenishment. These reduced precursors demonstrate that the NAD+ metabolic cycle is more flexible than initially recognized, providing alternative routes to boost NAD+ levels beyond the classic precursors tryptophan, nicotinamide, nicotinic acid, NMN, and NR, and supporting efforts to develop effective strategies for preventing NAD+ decline in aging and disease.

subject: SLC12A8
context: SLC12A8 is a transporter encoded by the gene SLC12A8 that has been proposed to mediate cellular uptake of nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), in addition to the CD73-mediated dephosphorylation route in which NMN is converted extracellularly to nicotinamide riboside for uptake. The expression of a gut transporter reinforces that NMN could be made bioavailable through oral delivery, and the presence of such a transporter in the intestine supports the idea that dietary NMN can enter the circulation. These uptake mechanisms complement each other and explain how orally administered NMN is rapidly absorbed from the intestine into the bloodstream and converted to NAD+ in tissues.

subject: NAAD
context: NAAD (nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide) is a product of NR utilization in humans and a biomarker of increased NAD+ metabolism. NR supplementation raised NAAD by 4.5-fold in blood, and healthy middle-aged adults taking 1 g/day NR for 6 weeks showed around a fivefold increase in blood NAAD. In another study, NAAD was undetectable before NR supplementation but increased by approximately 2,900% after single doses of up to 1 g NR. These findings corroborate studies in mice showing that the deamidated Preiss-Handler pathway predominates after NR intake, making NAAD a sensitive readout of the deamidated route of NAD+ precursor metabolism.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation substantially increases NAAD (nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide) levels, indicating flux through the deamidated Preiss-Handler pathway. Oral NR raised NAAD by 4.5-fold alongside more than twofold increases in NAD+ and 1.4-fold increases in NMN. Martens et al. reported about a fivefold increase in NAAD in blood of healthy middle-aged adults supplemented with 1 g/day NR for 6 weeks, and single doses of 100-1000 mg NR produced a roughly 2,900% increase in NAAD from undetectable baseline. NAAD is therefore a product and biomarker of NR metabolism that confirms the predominance of the deamidated route after NR intake.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: In an oncogenic mouse model, supplementation with NMN (500 mg/kg body weight daily for 13 days) significantly increased the secretory phenotype associated with pro-inflammatory senescence, promoting pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma progression. This raises the hypothesis that dietary supplements that increase NAD+ may be tumorigenic in vivo under stress conditions such as premalignant senescent lesions induced by activated oncogenes. The finding highlights the complex, context-dependent interplay between NAD+ metabolism and cancer biology, cautioning that NAD+ precursor supplementation could accelerate tumorigenesis in certain premalignant settings even as it confers health benefits in normal aging and metabolic disease.

subject: Combined Metabolic Activators
context: Combined metabolic activators (CMAs), consisting of NR (1 g), l-carnitine tartrate (3.73 g), N-acetylcysteine (2.55 g), and serine (12.35 g), improved COVID-19 outcomes in clinical trials. Patients taking the mixture orally for 14 days had significantly faster complete recovery times than placebo (6.6 vs 9.3 days in a phase 2 study and 5.7 vs 9.2 days in a phase 3 study). CMAs were found to reinforce the immune response and regulate amino acid and lipid metabolism, and patients showed improvements in plasma levels of inflammation and antioxidant metabolism-related biomarkers including alanine aminotransferase, lactate dehydrogenase, creatinine, glucose, and proteins. NR within the mixture contributes NAD+ restoration supporting antiviral PARP function.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: A case study of 10 critically ill COVID-19 patients over 50 years old reported that an NMN cocktail (83 mL of NMN mixed with 400 mL of water, consumed before breakfast and dinner) was strongly associated with resolution of COVID-19 symptoms. Before treatment, patients had low oxygen saturation, pulmonary infiltrates, and inflammation; post-treatment there was rapid improvement in bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, fever resolution, and lower inflammation biomarkers. One patient who stopped treatment after 3 days experienced relapse with fever and pulmonary infiltrates 8 days later. The rapid clinical improvement suggests NMN may help reverse the potentially fatal cytokine storm triggered by SARS-CoV-2, though larger controlled studies are needed.

subject: PARP
context: PARPs play a critical antiviral role by inhibiting the translation of viral transcripts through ADP-ribosylation of the viral genome, a process requiring NAD+. However, several viral families including SARS-CoV encode a macrodomain protein that hydrolyses the ADPR units from proteins and nucleic acids, inhibiting this PARP protective effect and facilitating replication and virulence. Excessive PARP activation then occurs to compensate for ADPR hydrolysis, accompanied by NAD+ consumption. This suggests that increasing NAD+ levels may restore the antiviral functions of PARPs to support immunity against SARS-CoV-2, providing a rationale for NAD+ precursor supplementation in COVID-19.

subject: SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain
context: The SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain is a viral protein that hydrolyses the ADP-ribose (ADPR) units added by PARPs to proteins and nucleic acids, thereby inhibiting the protective antiviral effect of PARPs and facilitating viral replication and virulence. Because PARPs require NAD+ to ADP-ribosylate viral transcripts, this counteraction leads to excessive PARP activation and NAD+ consumption during infection, dysregulating the NAD+ metabolome. Restoring NAD+ levels with precursors may therefore restore PARP antiviral function and support innate immunity to SARS-CoV-2, connecting NAD+ metabolism directly to COVID-19 severity and immune defense.

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 attenuates NF-kB signaling via histone H3 lysine 9 (H3K9) deacetylation at the chromatin of NF-kB target gene promoters, which are related to apoptosis and cellular senescence. Alongside SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT3, which suppress both NF-kB and NLRP3 inflammasome activity through multiple mechanisms, SIRT6 helps coordinate the intensity of inflammatory responses and prevent cytokine storms. Because sirtuins are NAD+-dependent, NAD+ precursor supplementation that raises NAD+ levels can reinforce this sirtuin-mediated restraint of NF-kB-driven inflammation, linking NAD+ metabolism to control of the pro-inflammatory transcription program during infection and aging.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) enhances aerobic capacity, as demonstrated in a randomized, double-blind study in amateur runners. NMN also improves mitochondrial function and energy metabolism: long-term administration in drinking water at 100 or 300 mg/kg/day for 12 months increased mitochondrial respiratory ability in skeletal muscle and reversed age-associated gene expression changes in a tissue-specific manner in aged mice. These mitochondrial and aerobic benefits are attributed to NMN raising NAD+ levels, which activates sirtuins and supports oxidative metabolism, energy expenditure, and oxygen consumption, positioning NMN as a performance- and healthspan-enhancing NAD+ precursor.

subject: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide
context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) rescues endothelial dysfunction associated with aging. In aged mice, intraperitoneal NMN at 500 mg/kg/day for 14 days reversed aging-induced cerebrovascular endothelial dysfunction and rescued neurovascular coupling responses, improving cognitive performance by increasing endothelial NO-mediated vasodilation. NMN also restored angiogenic capacity (capillary-like structure formation, proliferative and migratory capability) and attenuated oxidative stress in aged cerebromicrovascular endothelial cells. These vascular protective effects, which depend on NAD+ restoration and likely SIRT1 activation, prevent arterial and endothelial dysfunction and support NMN's role in preserving cardiovascular and cognitive health during aging.

subject: Hyperglycemia
context: The hallmark hyperglycemia of diabetes mellitus causes a redox imbalance between NAD+ and NADH that can lead to oxidative stress and a variety of metabolic syndromes. In cells whose glucose uptake is not insulin-dependent, glucose oversupply leads to NADH overproduction by both the conventional glucose combustion pathways (glycolysis and the Krebs cycle) and the polyol pathway. This NAD+/NADH imbalance, also known as pseudohypoxia, initially causes reductive stress and mitochondrial overload and dysfunction, which lead to oxidative stress and oxidative damage to DNA, lipids, and proteins. Additionally, PARP overactivation depletes NAD+, and this redox imbalance is a major factor contributing to the development of diabetic complications.

subject: CD38 knockdown
context: CD38 knockdown in mice suppressed axon degeneration, demyelination, and immune cell infiltration after facial nerve axotomy compared with wild-type mice, identifying CD38 as a candidate molecule for regulating neurodegeneration. Correspondingly, intraperitoneal injection of NR at 400 mg/kg once daily for 1 week prior to facial nerve axotomy delayed axon degeneration and demyelination and significantly increased NAD+ levels in the facial nucleus and facial nerve of wild-type mice. These findings connect the age-related rise in CD38 activity to NAD+ depletion and axonal vulnerability, and show that NAD+ precursor supplementation can mimic the protection achieved by CD38 deletion.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) delays axon degeneration and demyelination in a facial nerve axotomy model. Intraperitoneal injection of NR at 400 mg/kg once daily for 1 week prior to facial nerve axotomy delayed axon degeneration and demyelination and significantly increased NAD+ levels in the facial nucleus and facial nerve of wild-type mice, mimicking the protective effect of CD38 knockdown. Because the age-related increase in CD38 activity degrades NMN and NAD+ and alters precursor pharmacokinetics, NR-mediated NAD+ replenishment helps maintain axonal integrity after injury, supporting NR as a candidate intervention for neurodegeneration.

subject: Niacin
context: Nicotinic acid (niacin) at pharmacological doses reduces serum cholesterol levels in humans, but its clinical use is limited by a side effect of skin flushing accompanied by an unpleasant warmth sensation and often itching. Niacin, together with tryptophan and nicotinamide, is one of the classic NAD+ biosynthesis precursors historically used to prevent and treat pellagra, a disease characterized by dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia. Tryptophan alone is not sufficient to sustain cellular NAD+ levels because it participates in other metabolic pathways such as serotonin, melatonin, and picolinic acid synthesis, making nicotinic acid an important dietary NAD+ precursor with distinct pharmacological actions.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is one of the most studied nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) precursors, and it is the third NAD+ precursor discovered, naturally occurring in milk and already commercially available as a nutraceutical. Alongside nicotinamide (NAM), nicotinic acid (NA), and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), NR feeds into NAD+ biosynthetic salvage pathways and is regarded as a favorable precursor because it lacks the serious side effects and flushing attributed to other NAD+ precursors, and because its chloride salt has been granted GRAS (generally regarded as safe) status.

context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is a salvageable NAD+ precursor that forms NAD+ through a two-step or three-step pathway. subject: NMRK1
context: NMRK1 (nicotinamide ribose kinase 1), together with its isoform NMRK2, directly phosphorylates nicotinamide riboside (NR) to nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), bypassing the rate-limiting enzyme NAMPT. This route also circumvents the requirement for energetically costly PRPP (phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate) and the feedback inhibition by NAD+. NMRK1 is expressed ubiquitously across tissues, whereas NMRK2 expression is concentrated in cardiac and skeletal muscle, which helps explain why these tissues respond well to NR supplementation. NR is an orally available NAD+ precursor that increases NAD+ levels and sirtuin activity in multiple tissues.

subject: NAMPT
context: NAMPT (nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase) is the rate-limiting enzyme that converts nicotinamide (NAM), the most common NAD+ precursor in mammals, into nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN). This step requires more than three ATP equivalents, making it energetically more costly than the NMRK-mediated conversion of nicotinamide riboside (NR) to NMN, which needs only a single ATP. NAMPT expression and NAD+ content decline in multiple tissues with aging and overnutrition, and decreased NAMPT is a major cause of age-related NAD+ decline. NMN subsequently serves as the direct substrate for NMNAT, which generates the essential coenzyme NAD+.

subject: NMNAT
context: NMNAT (NMN/NaMN adenylyltransferases) catalyzes the final biosynthetic step in which nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is converted to the essential coenzyme NAD+. This step is shared by the salvage pathways from both nicotinamide riboside (NR) and nicotinamide (NAM): NR is first phosphorylated to NMN by NMRK1/NMRK2, while NAM is converted to NMN by NAMPT. NAD+ is required for glycolysis, fatty acid oxidation, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and it serves as the substrate for NAD+-consuming enzymes such as sirtuins and PARPs. Elevating NAD+ through precursor supplementation underlies the beneficial metabolic, cardiovascular, and neuroprotective effects attributed to NR.

subject: Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase
context: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase (NP) converts nicotinamide riboside (NR) into nicotinamide (NAM), which can then be converted back to NAD+ via NMN through the NAMPT and NMNAT enzymes. This NP-mediated cleavage is believed to be the variable step that degrades NR to NAM in the gut, potentially explaining the low and interindividually variable oral bioavailability of NR. NAM is the most common NAD+ precursor in mammals, and when administered at higher doses it can exert sirtuin-inhibiting effects. The balance between the direct NMRK pathway and this NP/NAMPT route determines how efficiently supplemented NR is converted to NAD+ in different tissues.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) bypasses the rate-limiting enzyme NAMPT because it is directly converted to nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) by the nicotinamide ribose kinases NMRK1 and NMRK2. This route circumvents the requirement for the energetically costly PRPP (phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate) and avoids the feedback inhibition that NAD+ exerts on its own synthesis, and it needs only a single ATP per NMN molecule compared to more than three ATP equivalents for NAMPT. NAMPT is the enzyme whose expression declines with age and in cardiac injury, and NR's ability to circumvent it underlies its therapeutic effects in heart failure and in NAD+-depleted tissues.

subject: Tryptophan
context: Tryptophan (Trp) is the dietary precursor for de novo NAD+ biosynthesis, which proceeds through an eight-step pathway that passes through quinolinic acid before generating NAD+. This de novo route complements the salvage pathways, which recycle nicotinamide (NAM), nicotinic acid (NA), nicotinamide riboside (NR), and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) back into NAD+ in two or three steps. Dietary tryptophan, or less than 20 mg of niacin daily, is sufficient to meet baseline NAD+ synthesis requirements, although greater rates of NAD+ synthesis through precursor supplementation are required to achieve therapeutic effects.

subject: NAD+
context: NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) is an essential coenzyme that plays central roles in cellular oxidation-reduction reactions, including most catabolic and anabolic processes such as glycolysis, fatty acid beta-oxidation, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and the synthesis of fatty acids, cholesterol, and steroids. Beyond its redox function, NAD+ is consumed by enzymes including sirtuins, poly-ADP-ribose polymerases (PARPs), CD38/CD157 ectoenzymes, and mono-ADP-ribose transferases, whose activity can deplete cellular NAD+ content.

subject: NAD+
context: Systemic NAD+ levels decline with aging as a result of both lowered rates of biosynthesis and increased consumption of NAD+. The decreased expression of the NAMPT enzyme is one of the major causes of this age-related NAD+ decline, and NAD+-consuming enzymes, including sirtuins, PARPs, and CD38, are induced by stress factors such as DNA damage, oxidative stress, and inflammation. The content of the primary mammalian NADase CD38 also increases with age, further lowering NAD+ availability. NAD+ depletion contributes to age-associated pathophysiology and is considered a major risk factor for Alzheimer's disease, supporting the use of NAD+ precursor supplementation to counter age-related decline.

subject: NAD+
context: NAD+ is indispensable for glycolysis because it serves as the electron acceptor in the oxidation of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate, and it participates in fatty acid beta-oxidation and the tricarboxylic acid cycle as a redox cofactor. This immense metabolic demand, spanning most catabolic and anabolic reactions including the synthesis of fatty acids, cholesterol, and steroids, drives the high turnover of NAD+ that must be met by de novo synthesis from tryptophan or by salvage pathways from nicotinamide (NAM), nicotinic acid (NA), nicotinamide riboside (NR), and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN).

subject: Sirtuins
context: Sirtuins are NAD+-dependent deacetylases/deacylases that function as conserved regulators of aging and longevity in diverse organisms and are regarded as the master switches of metabolism. They regulate metabolism, DNA repair, stress response, chromatin remodeling, and circadian rhythm, and their activity is absolutely dependent on NAD+ as a substrate. Sirtuin function is impaired when drastic NAD+ depletion occurs, as seen during maladaptive immune responses, and restoration of NAD+ levels through precursors such as nicotinamide riboside can restore sirtuin activity. In the heart, sirtuin activation mediates much of the cardioprotective benefit attributed to NAD+ precursor supplementation.
source_document: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md

subject: Sirtuins
context: Sirtuins, the NAD+-dependent deacetylases, are major downstream mediators of NAD+ biology and carry out numerous regulatory functions that include DNA repair, metabolism, stress response, chromatin remodeling, and circadian rhythm control. Because their deacetylase activity is absolutely dependent on NAD+, their function is sensitive to NAD+ depletion caused by aging and by consumption from PARPs and CD38. Supplementation with NAD+ precursors such as nicotinamide riboside can increase sirtuin activity, contributing to improved DNA repair, preserved mitochondrial function, and the beneficial metabolic and longevity effects documented in animal models.

subject: Sirtuins
context: Sirtuins are downregulated in the livers of patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), a condition characterized by hepatic steatosis and widely considered a hepatic manifestation of metabolic syndrome, since it is associated with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and insulin resistance. Because sirtuin activity is NAD+-dependent, raising NAD+ through nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation can restore sirtuin-driven fatty acid oxidation, inhibit lipogenesis, and reduce cholesterol levels, thereby improving liver health.
source_document: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md

subject: PARP1
context: PARP1, together with PARP2, is a poly-ADP-ribose polymerase that responds to DNA breaks in the nucleus and facilitates DNA repair by using NAD+ to build chains of ADP-ribose molecules. As DNA damage accumulates with age, PARP activation increases and competes with sirtuins for the shared NAD+ substrate, thereby lowering SIRT1 activity. PARP2 additionally binds the Sirt1 promoter and represses its expression. This PARP-mediated NAD+ depletion has been confirmed to play a major role in the pathogenesis of DNA repair disorders such as Cockayne syndrome, xeroderma pigmentosum, and ataxia-telangiectasia, and NAD+ precursor supplementation can improve these phenotypes in mouse models.
source_document: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md

subject: PARP2
context: PARP2 represses the expression of SIRT1 by binding to the promoter of the Sirt1 gene, and it competes with SIRT1 for the shared NAD+ substrate alongside PARP1. As DNA damage accumulates with age, increased PARP activation thereby lowers SIRT1 activity both through substrate competition and through this direct transcriptional repression. SIRT1 is an NAD+-dependent deacetylase whose activity is important for prevention of type 2 diabetes, preservation of insulin sensitivity, and healthy vascular function. Restoring NAD+ through precursor supplementation such as nicotinamide riboside can support SIRT1 activity and counteract the suppressive effects of PARP activation.
source_document: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md

subject: CD38
context: CD38 is the primary NADase in mammals, an ectoenzyme that uses NAD+ to produce and hydrolyze cADP-ribose, a Ca2+-mobilizing second messenger. Because CD38 also degrades the NAD+ intermediates nicotinamide riboside (NR) and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), its activity further decreases the content of NAD+. CD38 content increases with age, contributing to the age-related decline in NAD+ and mitochondrial dysfunction. In CD38-deficient mice, NAD+ levels remain high, preserving mitochondrial respiration and metabolic function with age, and pharmacological inhibition of CD38 can increase NAD+ levels and improve glucose and lipid metabolism.

subject: CD38
context: CD38, the primary NADase in mammals, degrades the NAD+ intermediates nicotinamide riboside (NR) and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), in addition to using NAD+ itself to produce and hydrolyze the Ca2+-mobilizing second messenger cADP-ribose. This degradation of NR and NMN further depletes cellular NAD+ content. CD38 expression increases with age and is also overexpressed in CD4+ and CD8+ lymphocytes upon activation of the adaptive immune response, which exaggerates NAD+ depletion. CD38-deficient mice maintain high NAD+ levels that preserve mitochondrial respiration and metabolic function with age, while CD38 inhibition increases NAD+ and improves glucose and lipid metabolism.

subject: CD38
context: The content of CD38, the primary NADase in mammals, increases with age, and this enzyme uses NAD+ to produce and hydrolyze the Ca2+-mobilizing second messenger cADP-ribose while also degrading the NAD+ intermediates nicotinamide riboside (NR) and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN). This age-related rise in CD38 therefore contributes to the progressive decline of NAD+ content during aging, and its effect was demonstrated in CD38-deficient mice whose NAD+ levels remain high, preserving mitochondrial respiration and metabolic function. Inhibition of CD38 can increase NAD+ levels and improve glucose and lipid metabolism, supporting NAD+ precursor strategies to counter age-associated decline.

subject: SARM1
context: SARM1 (sterile alpha and Toll/interleukin-1 receptor motif-containing 1) is an additional NAD+-depleting enzyme that uses NAD+ to promote axonal degeneration after injury, thereby decreasing overall NAD+ content. Axonal degeneration is an early event in acute cerebral injury and in chronic neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases, and it is caused by excitotoxicity, during which neurons undergo strong NAD+ depletion. Preserving axonal NAD+ to supply damage-induced SARM1 activation has been proposed as one of two mechanisms underlying the neuroprotective effects of nicotinamide riboside, which can protect neurons from excitotoxicity-induced axonal degeneration.

subject: CD73
context: CD73 is an ectoenzyme that converts NAD+ and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) extracellularly into nicotinamide riboside (NR), which then requires the NMRK pathway for cellular uptake and conversion back to NAD+. Because the utilization of NR and extracellular NAD+ is limited by the activity of the NMRK pathway, CD73-mediated extracellular processing is an important control point in NAD+ precursor biology. NR itself does not require conversion to enter cells, which partially explains its high availability, whereas NAD+ and its other precursors must be converted to either NR or NAM before entering the cell. A gut transporter for NMN encoded by the Slc12a8 gene has also been identified.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) administration increases the activity of SIRT1, an NAD+-dependent deacetylase that is important for the prevention of type 2 diabetes and the preservation of insulin sensitivity, and both SIRT1 and SIRT3 activities increased in vitro and in vivo in response to NR-induced NAD+ rises. SIRT1 inhibits the effects of oxidative stress in type 2 diabetic mice, promotes glucose-stimulated insulin secretion from pancreatic beta-cells, and protects against insulin resistance in peripheral tissues.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: In mouse models of high-fat-diet-induced obesity, a dietary dose of nicotinamide riboside (NR) as small as 400 mg/kg/day improved insulin sensitivity and protected mice from weight gain, while NR increased NAD+ metabolism, improved glucose tolerance, reduced weight gain, and exhibited neuroprotective effects against diabetic neuropathy and liver steatosis in diabetic mouse models. These rodent results have not yet been replicated in humans: 12-week supplementation of NR at 2000 mg/day did not improve insulin sensitivity or other metabolic parameters in insulin-resistant, obese men.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: In mouse models, nicotinamide riboside (NR) increases NAD+ metabolism and thereby improves glucose tolerance, reduces weight gain, and exhibits neuroprotective effects against diabetic neuropathy and liver steatosis. NR also restores the significantly decreased hepatic NADP+ and NADPH levels seen in prediabetic and type 2 diabetic mice, both of which are important for resistance to oxidative stress. These benefits are mediated in part through activation of SIRT1, which promotes glucose-stimulated insulin secretion from pancreatic beta-cells and protects against insulin resistance in peripheral tissues.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is a precursor not only of NADH but also of hepatic NADP+ and NADPH, and supplementation with NR restores the significantly decreased hepatic NADP+ and NADPH levels observed in prediabetic and type 2 diabetic mouse models. Both NADP+ and NADPH are important for resistance to oxidative stress, while NADPH is thought to be a major contributor to insulin resistance. Since the hepatic NAD+ metabolome reflects the progression of prediabetes and type 2 diabetes, NADP+ and NADPH can be used to assess disease progression, and their restoration by NR supports improved metabolic health and protection against diabetic complications such as neuropathy and liver steatosis.

This discrepancy highlights the need for additional research to determine the long-term effects of NR on insulin sensitivity in humans.

In regenerating liver, NR reduces lipid accumulation, promotes hepatocyte replication, and increases hepatic ATP content, leading to faster recovery of liver weight.

context: In the regenerating liver, nicotinamide riboside (NR) reduces lipid accumulation, promotes hepatocyte replication, and increases hepatic ATP content, leading to a faster regaining of liver weight in mice. This hepatoprotective and regenerative effect is tied to NAD+ biosynthesis, which supports the energy-producing and biosynthetic demands of liver regeneration. context: Dietary supplementation of nicotinamide riboside (NR) restored NAD+ levels caused by impaired biosynthesis in a mouse model of hepatocellular carcinoma and thereby prevented both DNA damage and tumorigenesis. NAD+ is required by sirtuins and PARPs that mediate DNA repair, and its depletion, driven by DNA damage and stress, is a feature of aging and age-associated pathology. By maintaining NAD+ availability for DNA repair enzymes and improving oxidative stress responses, NR displays beneficial effects on DNA repair in Alzheimer's disease mouse models as well. These findings support NR as a protective agent against genotoxic stress and tumorigenesis in the liver.

subject: Heart Failure

Activation of the NMRK2 pathway therefore represents a common adaptive mechanism in the failing heart, where NAD+ levels are low, and the Nmrk2 gene can be activated in response to NAMPT inhibition. This shift from NAMPT to NMRK2 for NAD+ synthesis is an energy-sparing mechanism, since NMN synthesis from NR by NMRK enzymes requires a single ATP while synthesis from NAM by NAMPT requires more than three ATP equivalents.

NR supplementation normalizes the myocardial NAD+/NADH ratio and, by improving NAD+ homeostasis and activating NMRK2, can prevent the deterioration of cardiac function and adverse remodeling in a mouse model of dilated cardiomyopathy leading to heart failure.

NR normalizes the myocardial NAD+/NADH ratio, and long-term supplementation increases nucleocytoplasmic protein acetylation by stimulating citrate and acetyl-CoA metabolism and antioxidant gene expression. In mouse models, NR-induced reduction of SBP and aortic stiffness was documented alongside improved NAD+ homeostasis.

subject: SIRT1
context: In vivo activation of SIRT1 protects against cardiac hypertrophy, metabolic dysregulation, and cardiac inflammation in a mouse model of cardiac hypertrophy, and exhibits protective effects in other models of cardiac dysfunction. SIRT1 is an NAD+-dependent deacetylase that mediates much of the cardioprotective benefit of NAD+ precursor supplementation, and NAD+ is an obligate substrate for its activity. In the failing heart, protein hyperacetylation driven by decreasing NAD+-dependent deacetylation increases both in mouse models of hypertrophy and in human patients with ischemic heart failure or dilated cardiomyopathy.

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 is a prominent cardioprotective sirtuin, as loss of SIRT6 in mice resulted in the development of cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure, while cardiac-specific SIRT6 overexpression protects the heart from hypertrophic stimuli by blocking activation of Akt signaling at the level of chromatin. Alongside SIRT1 and SIRT2, SIRT6 has emerged as a key mediator of the benefits of NAD+ precursor supplementation in the cardiovascular system. SIRT6 is a nuclear, chromatin-associated NAD+-dependent deacetylase involved in telomerase protection, genome stability, cholesterol homeostasis, and glucose metabolism.

subject: NMRK2
context: NMRK2 (nicotinamide ribose kinase 2) converts nicotinamide riboside (NR) to nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) using only a single molecule of ATP, whereas synthesis of NMN from nicotinamide by NAMPT requires more than three ATP equivalents. This makes the NMRK2 pathway an energy-sparing mechanism that may be favored in the failing heart, where the shift from NAMPT to NMRK2 for NAD+ synthesis represents a common adaptive response. NR is expressed and active mainly in cardiac and skeletal muscle, which may explain the better ability of these tissues to respond to NR. NR supplementation is therefore regarded as a powerful approach to preserve cardiac function in heart failure.

subject: NAD+ Depletion
context: NAD+ depletion was observed during the aging process in multiple animals, including humans, and is considered the major risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD). Neurodegenerative disorders such as AD are associated with DNA damage and oxidative stress, which accumulate with age and lead to impaired mitochondrial function, while excitotoxicity-driven axonal degeneration causes strong NAD+ depletion in neurons. When administered in AD mouse models, nicotinamide riboside (NR) displays beneficial effects on both oxidative stress and DNA repair by increasing NAD+ levels, and it improves pTau, amyloid-beta, neurogenesis, neuroinflammation, hippocampal synaptic plasticity, and cognition.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Since brain inflammation is closely related to cognitive impairment, nicotinamide riboside (NR) treatment reduced neuroinflammation and amyloidogenesis in the whole brain of high-fat-diet-fed mice by decreasing amyloid-beta levels and several inflammatory markers, and cognitive function and recognition memory could be attenuated by NR treatment within only 6 weeks. NR can improve multiple aspects of Alzheimer's disease neuropathology, including pTau, amyloid-beta, neurogenesis, neuroinflammation, hippocampal synaptic plasticity, and cognition, by increasing NAD+ levels and supporting DNA repair.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) treatment decreases IL-6 along with other inflammatory markers including NLRP3, CASP1, IL-1, and TNF-alpha in the whole brain of high-fat-diet-fed mice, contributing to reduced neuroinflammation and improved cognitive function. NR can similarly decrease IL-2, IL-5, IL-6, and TNF-alpha in human studies, and a 21-day supplementation of NR decreased numerous circulating inflammatory cytokines. Targeting IL-6 has been proposed as a promising treatment to block the inflammatory storm, especially in severe COVID-19 patients, supporting the potential of NR as an anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory agent in infection and age-related inflammatory conditions.
