subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Increased PARylation is a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, and it could be decreased in AD mice with nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation. Increased PARylation has also been detected in several other neurodegenerative disorders that involve DNA repair defects, including Cockayne syndrome, xeroderma pigmentosum, and ataxia-telangiectasia, where PARP-mediated NAD+ depletion plays a major role in pathogenesis. Despite the underlying DNA repair deficiencies, NR dramatically improved the phenotype of each of these conditions in mouse models, prolonging survival by more than three times in ataxic mice.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Among three tested NAD+ precursors (nicotinic acid, nicotinamide, and nicotinamide riboside) including NAD+ itself, only NR could prevent axonal degeneration by altering the local NR metabolism within the axon. Axonal degeneration is an early event in acute cerebral injury and in chronic neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases, and it is caused by excitotoxicity, which induces strong NAD+ depletion in neurons. NR prevented nuclear condensation and axonal degeneration in neurons of Nmrk2-KO mice by inducing Nmrk1, suggesting that Nmrk1 is a key mediator of the neuroprotective activity of NR.

subject: NMRK1
context: NR prevented nuclear condensation and axonal degeneration in neurons of Nmrk2-KO mice by inducing Nmrk1, which suggests that Nmrk1 (nicotinamide ribose kinase 1) might be the key mediator of the neuroprotective activity of nicotinamide riboside (NR). Two possible mechanisms of neuroprotection have been proposed: increasing mitochondrial NAD+ to support SIRT3 and preserving axonal NAD+ to supply damage-induced SARM1 activation. NMRK1 is expressed ubiquitously and converts NR to NMN in the salvage pathway for NAD+ synthesis. This neuroprotective role of NMRK1 supports the potential use of NR against excitotoxicity-induced axonal degeneration and neurodegeneration.
source_document: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) has been shown to prevent noise-induced hearing loss and neurite retraction from hair cells in the inner ear through a SIRT3-dependent mechanism, in which the NR-induced increase in NAD+ supports the activity of the mitochondrial deacetylase SIRT3. This illustrates the broader neuroprotective and therapeutic potential of NR, which also protects neurons from excitotoxicity-induced axonal degeneration and preserves axonal NAD+ content. SIRT3 activity is sensitive to the reduction of NAD+ content detected in multiple disorders with retinal degeneration, and NR may therefore have therapeutic applications for a variety of sensory and neurodegenerative conditions.

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 and SIRT5 are both critical for the health of retinal photoreceptors, and SIRT3 activity is sensitive to the reduction of NAD+ content detected in multiple disorders with retinal degeneration, including age-associated dysfunction, diabetic retinopathy, and light-induced degeneration in mice. SIRT3 is a mitochondrial NAD+-dependent deacetylase that supports ATP homeostasis, ROS detoxification, and neuroprotection, and increasing mitochondrial NAD+ to support SIRT3 is one proposed mechanism of nicotinamide riboside's neuroprotective effects. This suggests a potential therapeutic treatment with NR for a variety of disorders that include photoreceptor degeneration.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Oral supplementation with nicotinamide riboside (NR) is associated with improved mitochondrial function, and increasing NAD+ content with NR can stimulate energy production and improve mitochondrial abundance and function in two different mitochondrial myopathies, even though supplementation could not correct the underlying genetic defects. In mice, NR also confers increased endurance and improved cold tolerance in high-fat-diet-fed mice, while a nonsignificant trend toward increased endurance was seen in regular chow-fed mice.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) reversed the progressive wasting syndrome in skeletal muscle in mice lacking Nampt while restoring endurance in as little as 1 week of treatment. Decreased NAD+ levels and Nampt expression were also observed in Duchenne's muscular dystrophy (DMD), a condition histologically and transcriptionally similar to progressive wasting syndrome and characterized by increased PARP activity, fibrosis, and muscular degeneration. NR was found to improve muscular function and heart pathology in mdx mouse models of DMD and to decrease PARylation, inflammation, and fibrosis. These findings support NR as an effective approach to managing muscular dystrophy and degeneration.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: NR treatment has been shown to improve stem cell function and thereby ameliorate the muscle wasting phenotype in mdx mice, supporting the use of NR for the human condition of Duchenne's muscular dystrophy. Improvement in stem cell function appears to be a general phenomenon during NR treatment and has been suggested to underlie a small but significant extension of lifespan in mice. Oral supplementation with NR increases NAD+ levels in multiple tissues along with the regenerative potential of stem cells and improved mitochondrial function. These stem-cell-rejuvenating effects contribute to NR's beneficial profile for age-related tissue degeneration.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) was found to improve muscular function and heart pathology in mdx mouse models of Duchenne's muscular dystrophy (DMD) and to decrease PARylation, inflammation, and fibrosis. DMD is characterized by increased PARP activity, fibrosis, and muscular degeneration, and decreased NAD+ levels and Nampt expression are also observed in this condition. By improving muscular strength, rejuvenating senescent muscle stem cells, and reducing levels of inflammation and fibrosis, NR could be effective in managing the progression of muscular dystrophy and degeneration. These findings support the use of NR for the human condition of DMD.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Exogenous nicotinamide riboside (NR) promotes Sir2-dependent repression of recombination, improves gene silencing, and extends lifespan in yeast without calorie restriction, in the same manner as calorie restriction, which increases NAD+ levels and Sir2 function. The mechanism of action of NR in yeast is completely dependent on increased net NAD+ synthesis through the Nrk1 and the Urh1/Pnp1/4 pathways. A one-day fast increases NAD+ in the liver, and calorie restriction elevates NAD+ while reducing nicotinamide in the brain, implying that increased NAD+ mediates several beneficial effects of calorie restriction.

subject: Caloric Restriction
context: Calorie restriction (CR) is considered the most effective approach to extend lifespan in eukaryotes, and its life-prolonging effects may partly be mediated via increased sirtuin function, which requires NAD+ as a substrate. A study in mouse models documented that a one-day fast increases NAD+ in the liver, whereas CR elevates NAD+ and reduces nicotinamide in the brain, implying that increased levels of NAD+ mediate several beneficial effects of calorie restriction. As with CR, nicotinamide riboside (NR) can increase NAD+ levels and Sir2 function, and it extends lifespan in yeast without calorie restriction, supporting the life-prolonging effects of NR supplementation.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: A recent clinical study confirmed NR availability in muscular tissue in aged human subjects and demonstrated its anti-inflammatory effects, as a 21-day supplementation of NR decreased numerous circulating inflammatory cytokines. Preclinical studies reported that NR reduces macrophage infiltration in damaged muscles and attenuates plasma TNF-alpha in models of fatty liver disease. These effects are mediated via improvement of metabolism and a decrease in chronic inflammation, a hallmark of aging, and they imply additional mechanisms through which NR can modulate the aging process and exhibit life-prolonging effects.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Preclinical studies have reported that nicotinamide riboside (NR) reduces macrophage infiltration in damaged muscles and attenuates plasma TNF-alpha in models of fatty liver disease. These anti-inflammatory effects contribute to the improvement of metabolism and the decrease in chronic inflammation, a hallmark of aging, that underlie the life-prolonging benefits attributed to NR supplementation. subject: Niacin
context: Niacin was previously suggested as an anti-inflammatory therapy in a preclinical study as a potent agent to decrease proinflammatory cytokines, including IL-1, IL-6, and TNF-alpha, and it might also decrease neutrophil infiltration while exhibiting a prolonged anti-inflammatory effect during ventilator-induced lung injury. Nicotinamide riboside (NR) can similarly decrease IL-2, IL-5, IL-6, and TNF-alpha. Targeting IL-6 has been proposed as a promising treatment to block the inflammatory storm, especially in severe COVID-19 patients.

subject: Vitamin B3
context: High efficiency of vitamin B3 (niacin or nicotinamide) in preventing lung tissue damage was confirmed in several animal models with bleomycin- and LPS-induced lung injury, and considering this strong lung-protective effect, vitamin B3 has been proposed as an early treatment-supporting agent against COVID-19, which otherwise causes a maladaptive hyperinflammatory response with a cytokine storm in lung tissue. Nicotinamide riboside (NR), as a vitamin B3 derivative, is therefore considered a potential therapeutic or supporting agent to reduce hyperinflammation and regenerate damaged lung tissue during SARS-CoV-2 infection, where excess leucocyte infiltration causes extensive tissue damage

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is very unstable in the blood, which makes it difficult to measure and detect, and this instability is partially due to degradation of NR to nicotinamide (NAM), compromising its ability to reach peripheral tissues after oral administration. Despite this instability, the development of reliable methods for collection, processing, and measurement has enabled determination of the pharmacokinetic profile of orally administered NR, and the apparent oral bioavailability of a 1000 mg dose of NR is highly variable among individuals. The reduced form of NR, NRH, appears more stable than NR and does not undergo direct degradation in plasma.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: In response to nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation, a remarkable increase (45-fold) in nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide (NAAD) was reported in a study with male human subjects and C57Bl6/J mice, indicating an additional conversion pathway of NR to NAD+. NAAD represents the most sensitive biomarker of effective NAD+ supplementation since it is undetectable in the blood prior to supplementation and its levels increase in the liver after orally administered NAD+ precursors. NR could also significantly elevate NAAD heart content, where the increase of NAD+ occurs in the absence of a steady-state NAD+ increase, and NR increased NAAD by at least 45-fold compared to baseline.

subject: NRH
context: NRH, the reduced form of nicotinamide riboside, is bioavailable in mice and increases NAD+ in both cultured cells (5-10-fold above the baseline) and in mice, in a more potent and faster manner than NR, and it is detectable in circulation after oral intake or intraperitoneal injection. A NMRK-independent pathway for the NRH-induced NAD+ increase has been demonstrated, consistent with the recent discovery of a novel biosynthetic route of NAD+ from NRH through the NMNH intermediate, where adenosine kinase (ADK) acts as an NRH kinase. The presence of endogenous NRH in the liver of mouse models was confirmed, establishing NRH as a valid natural precursor of NAD+.

subject: Adenosine Kinase
context: Adenosine kinase (ADK) acts as an NRH kinase in a recently discovered novel biosynthetic route of NAD+ from NRH (the reduced form of nicotinamide riboside) through the NMNH intermediate, providing a NMRK-independent pathway for the NRH-induced NAD+ increase. NRH is more stable than nicotinamide riboside (NR), which degrades to nicotinamide in the blood, and NRH increases NAD+ in both cultured cells (5-10-fold above the baseline) and mice, in a more potent and faster manner than NR. Endogenous NRH was detected in the liver of mouse models, establishing NRH as a valid natural precursor of NAD+.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) administration can elevate NAD+ levels in mammalian cells and tissues without activating GPR109A, the receptor that mediates nicotinic acid-induced flushing, which is why NR is not associated with the painful flushing side effect seen with niacin. Although nicotinic acid (NA) and nicotinamide (NAM) can enter the NAD+ salvage pathway, several preclinical studies have confirmed that both can cause painful flushing sensations at therapeutic doses or other toxic effects. NR, in contrast, was confirmed across a number of studies as well-tolerated up to 2 g of a daily dose, with no flushing or severe side effects reported.

subject: Nicotinic acid
context: Nicotinic acid (NA, niacin) is implicated with flushing at doses higher than 50 mg/day, and several preclinical studies have confirmed that both NA and nicotinamide (NAM) can cause painful flushing sensations at therapeutic doses or other toxic effects. NA shows lowering effects on blood lipid levels and is used to treat dyslipidemia, but this flushing side effect limits its tolerability. In contrast, nicotinamide riboside (NR) elevates NAD+ levels without activating GPR109A, the receptor that mediates nicotinic acid-induced flushing, and was confirmed across a number of studies as well-tolerated up to 2 g of a daily dose, with no flushing or severe side effects.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Among the three precursors nicotinic acid (NA), nicotinamide (NAM), and nicotinamide riboside (NR), only NR could prolong survival and induce hematopoietic stem cell regeneration, as documented in a study with mice treated with irradiation. This implies advantages of the NR precursor for potential use in cancer patients undergoing chemo- or radiotherapy, and orally administered NR was also found to improve resistance to and reversal of chemotherapeutic neuropathy. NR's ability to rejuvenate stem cells appears to be a general phenomenon during treatment and has been suggested to underlie a small but significant extension of lifespan in mice.
source_document: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md

subject: Nicotinic acid
context: Nicotinic acid (NA, niacin) shows lowering effects on blood lipid levels, and it is used to treat dyslipidemia, although it is implicated with flushing at doses higher than 50 mg/day. In contrast, nicotinamide (NAM) does not affect lipid blood levels, yet it can exhibit sirtuin-inhibiting effects at higher doses, while nicotinamide riboside (NR) does not cause flushing because it does not activate GPR109A. The distinct physiological responses of the NAD+ precursors NA, NAM, and NR, despite all three raising NAD+ and NADP+ levels, are important for selecting the appropriate precursor for specific therapeutic indications.

subject: Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease
context: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is widely considered a hepatic manifestation of metabolic syndrome as it is found to be associated with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and insulin resistance, and sirtuins are downregulated in NAFLD patients, a state characterized by liver steatosis. Raising NAD+ through nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation can restore sirtuin-driven fatty acid oxidation, inhibit lipogenesis, and reduce cholesterol levels, thereby improving liver health and reducing fat accumulation through induction of the mitochondrial unfolded protein response.

subject: NRH
context: Since nicotinamide riboside (NR) is unstable in blood circulation, partially due to degradation to nicotinamide, its ability to reach peripheral tissues after oral administration is compromised, and this limitation could be overcome by the administration of NRH, the reduced form of NR, which appears to be more stable than NR and does not undergo direct degradation in plasma. NRH is detectable in circulation after oral intake or intraperitoneal injection, and it increases NAD+ in both cultured cells (5-10-fold above the baseline) and mice, in a more potent and faster manner than NR, through a NMRK-independent pathway in which adenosine kinase acts as an NRH kinase.

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 promotes glucose-stimulated insulin secretion from pancreatic beta-cells, inhibits the effects of oxidative stress in type 2 diabetic mice, and protects against insulin resistance in peripheral tissues, and it is an NAD+-dependent deacetylase whose activity is increased by nicotinamide riboside (NR) administration. SIRT1 overexpression also promotes fatty acid oxidation and inhibits lipogenesis, protecting the liver from steatosis, and sirtuins are downregulated in patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

subject: Nicotinamide Riboside
context: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is the third discovered NAD+ precursor and naturally occurs in milk, and it is already available as a nutraceutical, with its chloride salt given GRAS (generally regarded as safe) status. NAD+ intermediates such as NR are found in a wide variety of foods, including meat, eggs, dairy, certain vegetables, and whole wheat, and high availability of NR has been observed in the normal human diet. Oral supplementation with NR has been shown to increase NAD+ levels in multiple tissues along with increased sirtuin activity, improved mitochondrial function, and regenerative potential of stem cells, making NR a leading candidate among NAD+ precursors.
source_document: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A (UA) is a naturally occurring compound classified within the urolithins, a family of gut-microbiota-derived metabolites that form when dietary polyphenols are processed in the gastrointestinal tract. The review describes urolithins as compounds present in pomegranates and certain other fruits and nuts such as strawberries, walnut kernels, and peanuts, with ellagitannins serving as their precursors. As a member of this family, Urolithin A has attracted considerable research attention due to its pharmacological effects, encompassing anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-tumor, and anti-aging properties, and it is a primary focus of research into muscle health and performance.

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A is a natural metabolite derived from ellagitannins, polyphenolic precursors found in pomegranate, walnut, almond, strawberry, and blueberry. During digestion, microbial enzymes in the colon convert ellagitannins through stepwise enzymatic and metabolic reactions to yield urolithin A. Because ellagitannin intake is a precondition for urolithin A formation, dietary consumption of ellagitannin-rich foods supplies an abundance of precursor molecules for intestinal microbial metabolism, facilitating the generation of urolithin A and increasing its systemic availability.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Gut Microbiome
context: The production of urolithin A depends largely on the metabolic activities of the gut microbiota. During digestion, polyphenolic compounds such as tannins and anthocyanins undergo enzymatic reactions and metabolic conversions facilitated by microbial enzymes, culminating in the production of urolithin A. This metabolism predominantly takes place in the colon, which houses a variety of microbial groups including Proteobacteria, Clostridium, Bifidobacterium, Eubacterium, and Enterococcus faecium that possess distinct metabolic functions, so individual differences in intestinal microbial composition influence how much urolithin A a person produces and absorbs.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Pomegranate
context: Pomegranate is cited as one of the primary and richest dietary sources of urolithin A. Pomegranate peel and seeds contain abundant polyphenolic compounds, including ellagitannins that are metabolized by the gut microbiota into urolithin A. Consequently, consuming pomegranate supplies an abundance of precursor molecules for intestinal microbial metabolism, facilitating the generation of urolithin A, and pomegranate consumption is a standard dietary route to increase systemic urolithin A exposure alongside other sources such as walnut, almond, strawberry, and blueberry.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Liver
context: Once absorbed into the circulation, urolithin A undergoes further metabolism through multiple metabolic pathways, with the liver playing a central role. Metabolic enzymes present in the liver convert urolithin A into its mercaptan and sulfate forms. Hepatic enzyme inducers such as rifampicin and carbamazepine can increase the activity of these metabolic enzymes, accelerating urolithin A metabolism and reducing its half-life in the body, whereas enzyme inhibitors such as clarithromycin slow its metabolism and clearance and can lead to accumulation of urolithin A.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Kidney
context: Urolithin A and its metabolites can be excreted from the body through the kidneys and intestines. Renal function can influence the rate of urolithin A elimination, since a portion of the compound and its conjugated forms is cleared in the urine, while additional urolithin A is further metabolized into other compounds within the intestines before being eliminated through feces. Renal function, intestinal permeability, and individual characteristics are therefore among the physiological factors that shape the bioavailability, metabolism, and distribution of urolithin A.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Rifampicin
context: Rifampicin is a hepatic enzyme inducer that can increase the activity of certain metabolic enzymes in the liver, potentially accelerating the metabolism of urolithin A and reducing its half-life in the body. This illustrates the broader principle that drugs interacting with cytochrome P450 enzymes in the liver can competitively inhibit or induce these enzymes, thereby disrupting the metabolism and clearance of urolithin A and altering its systemic exposure. Common antibiotics, antifungal drugs, and anticancer drugs have been reported to interact with CYP450 enzymes in this way.

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A activates the PINK1/Parkin signaling pathway involved in mitochondrial quality control. Activation of this pathway promotes selective aggregation, degradation, and removal of damaged mitochondria, and PINK1 is one of the principal regulatory proteins mediating mitophagy. By engaging PINK1-dependent signaling, urolithin A enhances the clearance of dysfunctional mitochondria, an effect central to its characterization as a mitophagy activator and to its reported benefits for mitochondrial health, muscle function, and prevention of cellular degeneration.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: PINK1
context: Mitochondrial autophagy, also known as mitophagy, refers to the selective degradation of mitochondria through the autophagic process, and its regulation is mediated by proteins such as PINK1 and Parkin. PINK1 is a key sensor of mitochondrial damage that recruits Parkin to trigger degradation of dysfunctional organelles, maintaining mitochondrial turnover and homeostasis. Urolithin A activates this PINK1/Parkin signaling pathway to promote the selective aggregation, degradation, and removal of damaged mitochondria, thereby supporting mitochondrial quality control and cellular health.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A activates mitochondrial autophagy (mitophagy), the selective degradation of damaged or defective mitochondria that maintains mitochondrial turnover and homeostasis. It promotes this process by activating the PINK1/Parkin signaling pathway and by upregulating glutathione S-transferases via the NRF2-ARE signaling pathway, thereby enhancing cellular autophagy and mitochondrial quality control. This mitophagy-activating activity is central to urolithin A's reported effects on mitochondrial health, muscle energy metabolism, and the prevention of dysfunctional mitochondrial accumulation that could otherwise lead to cellular degeneration.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A stimulates the NRF2-Antioxidant Response Element (ARE) signaling pathway, which upregulates the expression of antioxidant and detoxifying enzymes such as glutathione S-transferases (GSTs). Through this Nrf2 antioxidant pathway, urolithin A enhances cellular antioxidant defense, supports cellular autophagy and mitochondrial quality control, and reduces oxidative stress. NRF2 activation is a recurring mechanism underlying urolithin A's antioxidant and cytoprotective actions across multiple cell types, including its reported ability to protect muscle cells during strenuous exercise.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: NRF2
context: NRF2, acting through the Antioxidant Response Element, upregulates the expression of glutathione S-transferases (GSTs), which are pivotal detoxifying enzymes intricately related to antioxidant capacity. This transcriptional program, stimulated in the setting of urolithin A treatment, enhances cellular autophagy and mitochondrial quality control. GSTs are therefore downstream effectors of NRF2 signaling that help protect cells against oxidative and electrophilic stress and that support the removal and turnover of damaged mitochondria.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A possesses the ability to directly scavenge free radicals by capturing and neutralizing reactive oxygen species such as peroxy radicals and superoxide radicals, thereby reducing cellular oxidative stress. This direct radical-scavenging activity, together with its ability to activate the Nrf2 antioxidant pathway and upregulate antioxidant enzymes such as glutathione peroxidase and superoxide dismutase, underpins urolithin A's classification as an antioxidant compound. During exercise, when the body generates excessive ROS that can damage cellular structures, this scavenging protects muscle cells and supports muscle health.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A reduces cellular oxidative stress through multiple mechanisms: it directly scavenges reactive oxygen species such as peroxy and superoxide radicals, activates the Nrf2 antioxidant pathway to upregulate enzymes like glutathione peroxidase and superoxide dismutase, and inhibits enzyme activities involved in ROS generation. During exercise, especially strenuous activities, the body is more susceptible to generating excessive ROS, and urolithin A lowers the level of oxidative stress within muscle cells, protecting cellular structures and functions and thereby promoting muscle health.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A can regulate the cell cycle by inhibiting the activity of cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) and reducing the expression of cell cycle proteins such as cyclin D1, leading to cell cycle arrest in the G1 phase. It also increases the levels of cell cycle inhibitory proteins such as p21 and p27. This cell-cycle control, achieved through modulation of CDK activity and cyclin expression, contributes to urolithin A's reported antiproliferative activity and to its effects on cell cycle-related protein kinase complexes.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A can regulate the cell cycle by increasing the levels of cell cycle inhibitory proteins such as p21 and p27, complementing its inhibition of cyclin-dependent kinase activity and its reduction of cyclin D1 expression. Elevation of these cell cycle inhibitory proteins promotes cell cycle arrest in the G1 phase. Together these effects define urolithin A's capacity to modulate cell cycle progression, a property with relevance to its anti-tumor and antiproliferative activity in cancer contexts.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A can induce cell death through multiple pathways. Studies have found that urolithin A increases the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, resulting in the loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, release of cytochrome c, and activation of the caspase cascade, ultimately leading to cell apoptosis. It also activates the JNK (c-Jun N-terminal kinase) and p38 MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase) signaling pathways, further promoting apoptosis. These pro-apoptotic effects underpin urolithin A's anti-tumor activity and its ability to regulate cell death in various contexts.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A induces apoptosis by increasing the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, which results in the loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, release of cytochrome c, and activation of the cascade of caspases, ultimately leading to cell apoptosis. Modulation of the pro-apoptotic to anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family ratio is a classical intrinsic (mitochondrial) apoptosis trigger. It represents one of the several mechanisms through which urolithin A promotes programmed cell death, in addition to its activation of JNK and p38 MAPK signaling.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Cytochrome c
context: Upon loss of mitochondrial membrane potential induced by an increased Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, cytochrome c is released from mitochondria and activates the cascade of caspases, ultimately leading to cell apoptosis. This mitochondrial intrinsic pathway of apoptosis is engaged by urolithin A as part of its pro-apoptotic actions. Cytochrome c release and subsequent activation of executioner caspases are central to intrinsic cell death signaling downstream of mitochondrial permeabilization and contribute to the anti-tumor activity reported for urolithin A.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: Urolithin A
context: Urolithin A activates the AMPK (adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase) signaling pathway, a pivotal regulator of energy metabolism. The literature demonstrates that urolithin A activates AMPK through a cascade involving the activation of SIRT3 and, subsequently, LKB1. AMPK activation promotes fatty acid oxidation and insulin sensitivity while reducing fatty acid synthesis and gluconeogenesis, and it can increase mitochondrial biogenesis and glycogen synthesis, ultimately improving muscle energy supply and metabolism and enhancing muscle performance.
source_document: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md

subject: AMPK
context: Activation of AMPK promotes fatty acid oxidation and insulin sensitivity while reducing fatty acid synthesis and gluconeogenesis, and it can also increase mitochondrial biogenesis and glycogen synthesis. Through AMPK-dependent signaling, urolithin A improves muscle energy supply and metabolism. subject: Persulfates
context: Persulfates are employed as the oxidizing agent to convert adrenaline (epinephrine) into adrenochrome. The use of persulfates is advantageous because it precludes the effluent disposal problems associated with potassium ferricyanide and is significantly cheaper, although persulfate oxidation alone is slow and requires catalysts such as water-soluble bismuth salts. Suitable persulfates include potassium persulfate, sodium persulfate, and ammonium persulfate, with the sodium and ammonium salts preferred for their good solubility in water.

subject: Bismuth
context: Water-soluble salts of bismuth, such as bismuth nitrate, bismuth oxynitrate, bismuth oxycarbonate, and bismuth citrate, accelerate the persulfate oxidation of adrenaline into adrenochrome, producing high-quality adrenochrome in high yields in a short period of time (about 30 to 45 minutes). Bismuth salts are used in amounts of 0.001 to 0.01 mole per mole of adrenaline; amounts below this do not significantly increase the reaction rate, while amounts above 0.01 mole may cause excessive oxidation and decompose the adrenochrome into tar-like by-products.

The carbazochrome obtained by the bismuth-catalyzed persulfate method is far less colored than that prepared using the potassium ferricyanide method, and its identity is confirmed by UV absorption at 354 nm and characteristic infrared absorptions.

subject: Carbazochrome
context: Carbazochrome (adrenochrome monosemicarbazone) is known as a hemostatic agent, one of two hydrazine derivatives of adrenochrome described in the patent, the other being adrenochrome monoaminoguanidine. These hydrazine derivatives serve both for the stabilization of adrenochrome and for the preparation of useful medicines that act to stop bleeding. In the patented process, semicarbazide is added to the adrenochrome solution at 0 to 15 degrees C at pH 5 to 7 to form carbazochrome, which is then isolated by filtration and purified.

subject: Adrenochrome monoaminoguanidine
context: Adrenochrome monoaminoguanidine is a hemostatic agent formed by reacting aminoguanidine with adrenochrome, an unstable ortho-quinoid intermediate. Along with carbazochrome, it is one of the hydrazine derivatives of adrenochrome that serve as useful medicines with hemostatic activity. In the patented process, stabilization with aminoguanidine is carried out at pH 2 to 5, and the purified compound shows characteristic ultraviolet absorption maxima at 348 nm and 445 nm that confirm its identity. The product is isolated by filtration, washed and dried to a powder, and may be further purified by active carbon treatment and recrystallization.

subject: Potassium ferricyanide
context: Adrenochrome has been commercially prepared by oxidizing adrenaline or its salts with potassium ferricyanide in an aqueous medium. This process is uneconomical because of the large quantities of potassium ferricyanide needed, the ensuing effluent disposal problems, and variability in product quality. The patent presents a bismuth-catalyzed persulfate process as a superior alternative that precludes these problems and yields less-colored carbazochrome and adrenochrome monoaminoguanidine products.

subject: Hydrazines
context: Adrenochrome is very unstable due to its ortho-quinoid structure and is therefore usually stabilized by conventional derivatization with hydrazines, e.g., aminoguanidine, semicarbazide, phenylhydrazine, o-nitrophenylhydrazine, p-nitrophenylhydrazine, and 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine. These hydrazine derivatives serve both for the stabilization of adrenochrome and for the preparation of useful medicines such as hemostatics. The stabilization treatment is generally conducted for 30 minutes to 3 hours at a temperature of 0 to 15 degrees C.

subject: Aminoguanidine
context: Aminoguanidine reacts with adrenochrome to form adrenochrome monoaminoguanidine, a hemostatic agent. In the patented process, an aqueous aminoguanidine hydrochloride solution is added to the adrenochrome reaction mixture at below 5 degrees C, the pH is adjusted to about 2.9 for the stabilization step, and the product is precipitated at a final pH of 9.0 to 10.0 with sodium hydroxide. The reaction yields about 41.0 g of crude product that is purified by dissolving in sulfurous acid, active carbon treatment, and the addition of EDTA, and the purified compound shows ultraviolet absorption maxima at 348 nm and 445 nm.

subject: Semicarbazide
context: Semicarbazide reacts with adrenochrome to form adrenochrome monosemicarbazone (carbazochrome), a hemostatic agent. In the patented process, semicarbazide hydrochloride is added to the adrenochrome solution at below 10 degrees C in the presence of a potassium acetate buffer, with the stabilization carried out at pH 5 to 7. The reaction yields about 40.0 g of crude powder that is purified by dissolving in dilute sodium hydroxide, active carbon treatment, and precipitation at pH 5.5, and the purified product shows an ultraviolet absorption maximum at 354 nm and characteristic infrared absorptions matching those of an authentic sample.

subject: Sodium hydrogencarbonate
context: The aqueous reaction medium for adrenochrome synthesis is maintained at a pH from 4 to 8, preferably with a buffer such as sodium hydrogencarbonate, sodium dihydrogenphosphate, disodium hydrogenphosphate, potassium acetate, or sodium acetate, with sodium hydrogencarbonate being preferred. The buffer is generally used in an amount of 4 to 7 moles, preferably 5 to 6 moles, per mole of adrenaline. Maintaining this pH range supports the persulfate oxidation of adrenaline catalyzed by water-soluble bismuth salts.

subject: Adrenochrome
context: Adrenochrome is very unstable due to its ortho-quinoid (o-quinone) structure, and is therefore usually stabilized by conventional derivatization with hydrazines such as aminoguanidine and semicarbazide to form hemostatic medicines. This instability also means that during the persulfate oxidation of adrenaline, the produced adrenochrome may be further oxidized and decompose to black by-products, so the reaction is monitored by sampling and measuring the absorbance at 495 nm, which is stopped at the point of maximum yield.

subject: Ammonium Persulfate
context: Ammonium persulfate is one of the suitable persulfate oxidizing agents for converting adrenaline into adrenochrome, together with potassium persulfate and sodium persulfate. Sodium and ammonium persulfates are preferred over potassium persulfate for their good solubility in water. In the examples, ammonium persulfate (about 0.42 mole) is used with a sodium hydrogencarbonate buffer and a bismuth salt catalyst at 0 to 5 degrees C to produce adrenochrome in maximum yield within about 30 to 45 minutes.

subject: Adrenochrome
context: During the oxidation of adrenaline, the reaction mixture is tinged with purplish red due to the production of adrenochrome, and its color becomes deeper with increasing adrenochrome content. The reaction is continued until the absorbance at a wavelength of 495 nm, measured by sampling the reaction mixture at an appropriate time, reaches a maximum, at which point further oxidation of the product is minimized and adrenochrome is obtained in maximum yield. The reaction time required for maximum yield varies from 30 to 45 minutes depending on the temperature of the reaction mixture and the level of catalyst employed.
